HowMaHiCo

A parameterized RMarkdown reporting workflow for LC-immunopeptidomics (MHC/HLA peptide) data analysis. It ingests LC-MS search-engine output from multiple tools (FragPipe, DIA-NN, PEAKS), normalizes it into a single unified long-format table (pep_all), and renders self-contained, interactive HTML QC reports plus csv/xlsx result exports.

Distributed as an R package (mid-conversion, on the dev branch — see project-style-guide.md for the target R-package + Docker + Shiny distribution pattern). library(HowMaHiCo) gives you the full function library and the report templates; this repo also serves as a worked example of the analysis pattern — useful as a reference for setting up similar immunopeptidomics QC pipelines.

What it does 

LC-MS search output (FragPipe psm.tsv, DIA-NN report.tsv, PEAKS peptide.csv)
      │   read + parse + annotate  (software-specific loaders converge on one schema)
      ▼
pep_all  — unified long-format peptide table
      │
      ▼
inst/rmarkdown/templates/00_mhc_report/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd
      │   rendered via run_howmahico_report() — self-contained interactive HTML
      │   (ID counts, replicate/condition overlaps, size & charge distributions,
      │    RT/ion-mobility/m_z "pseudochromatograms", Area correlation & %CV,
      │    Score/ppm QC, sequence motifs, PTM profile)
      ▼
csv / xlsx result tables  +  optional PNG figure exports

Each report is rendered once per analysis subset (e.g. acquisition mode × sample group), driven by an annotation CSV that maps raw data files to experimental conditions and replicates.

Repository layout

Folder Contents
R/ Package source — the ~40 functions (loaders, annotation, counting, plotting, export) plus the run_howmahico_report()/derive_filtered_annotation() entry points
inst/rmarkdown/templates/ The parameterized Rmd report templates — 00_mhc_report (all-in-one), 00_mhc_upsets, and the focused 01_id_counts/02_overlaps/03_lcms_qc/04_quant/05_quality_score/06_quant_stats — packaged for rmarkdown::draft()/run_howmahico_report(). Shared setup for the focused reports lives in inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd
tests/testthat/ testthat-edition-3 suite (hand-synthesized fixtures — never derived from real instrument data)
man/ Generated roxygen2 documentation (.Rd)
1_documentation/ Sample annotation CSVs (one per analysis subset)
2_data/ Raw search-engine output + cached pep_all (not tracked — see .gitignore)
3_results/ Generated csv/xlsx result tables (not tracked)
4_figures/ Optional generated PNG plot exports (not tracked)
example/ Legacy pre-package reference copies — gitignored, for reference only

2_data/, 3_results/, 4_figures/, and the rendered *.html reports are regenerated by running the pipeline and are excluded from version control — see .gitignore.

Requirements

  • R (>= 4.1.0) with RStudio (project file: HowMaHiCo.Rproj)
  • Install the package (e.g. devtools::install_github("DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo") or devtools::load_all() from a clone) — all dependencies are declared in DESCRIPTION (Imports/Suggests) and resolved automatically; no manual library list or companion-package install required

How to run

1. Install the package

# from a local clone:
devtools::load_all()
# or from GitHub:
devtools::install_github("DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo")
library(HowMaHiCo)

2. Auto-generate an annotation CSV skeleton

# FragPipe (psm.tsv layout)
get_annot_fragpipe(dir_data = "2_data") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")

# DIA-NN (report.tsv layout)
get_annot_diann(dir_data = "2_data") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation_diann.csv")

# PEAKS (export folders)
get_annot_peaks(dir_data = "2_data/peaks_export") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation_peaks.csv")

These scan 2_data and write one row per data file — no sample_list.xlsx needed to get started (Sample_ID can be filled in next, by hand or optionally from a HyStar sample list).

3. Complete the annotation CSV

Open the generated CSV and fill in the experimental metadata: Condition, BioReplicate, TechReplicate, Sample_ID. Verify that Sample_folder matches the data subfolder names exactly, then save. The column is the same for every search engine; tables from older runs that use the engine-specific Sample_fp (FragPipe/DIA-NN) or Sample_peaks (PEAKS) still load unchanged.

Two things the annotation table controls: - Inclusion — only samples listed in the annotation table are read and reported. Any sample present in the results folder but missing from the table is silently excluded, so the table is also how you subset a run. - Ordering — Conditions, replicates and samples appear in every plot and table in the row order of the annotation CSV. Order the rows the way you want them displayed (factor levels are taken from first appearance).

(Optional) Sample_ID can be populated automatically from a Bruker HyStar sample list with get_annot_sampleid() instead of typing it by hand:

read.csv("1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv") |>
  get_annot_sampleid(file_sample_list = "1_documentation/sample_list.xlsx") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")

get_annot_sampleid() joins on Source_file, so both sides must use the same run naming. It warns when nothing matched (showing example values from each side) and when only some rows matched (naming the dropped ones); pass keep_all = TRUE to keep every annotation row instead, with the unmatched Sample_ID left empty.

4. (Optional) Get a local copy of the report template to customise

get_report_template("MyReport", template = "00_mhc_report")

5. Render a report

Edit these for your run (the rest can stay at the example defaults):

  • SampleSet / Subset — experiment name and subset label (used in the title, filenames, and output subfolders)
  • FolderDocumentation / FolderData / FolderResults / FolderFigures — absolute (or render-time-cwd-relative) paths
  • AnnotationFile — the CSV filled in above
  • Software — fragpipe_dda_combined | fragpipe_dda_individual | diann | peaks_xpro | custom
  • Instrument — tims_tof | faims_orbi | orbi
  • MHCclass — MHC1 (human, 8–13 AA), MHC1_mouse (murine H-2, 7–11 AA) or MHC2 (12–25 AA)
  • output_file — the HTML filename to write

See the full parameter reference (incl. PepAllSource, TestMode, ResultsOverwrite, CsvSave/PlotsSave) in CLAUDE.md.

run_howmahico_report(
  template = "00_mhc_report",          # or "00_mhc_upsets"
  params = list(
    Title            = "MHC1 immunopeptidomics — DDA all",
    SampleSet        = "project_id",
    DataAnalysisNames = "DGZ",
    WetLabNames      = "operator",
    FolderDocumentation = "1_documentation",
    AnnotationFile   = "sample_annotation.csv",
    Subset           = "dda_all",
    FolderData       = "2_data",
    FolderResults    = "3_results",
    FolderFigures    = "4_figures",
    # ProjectDir     = getwd(),   # set if rendering from a subdirectory
    Instrument       = "tims_tof",    # faims_orbi | orbi
    Software         = "fragpipe_dda_combined",
    MHCclass         = "MHC1",        # MHC1 (8-13 AA) | MHC1_mouse (7-11 AA) | MHC2 (12-25 AA)
    TestMode         = FALSE,
    ResultsOverwrite = TRUE,
    PlotsSave        = FALSE,
    CsvSave          = FALSE
  ),
  output_file = "01_report_main__hla1_dda_all.html"
)

FolderDocumentation/FolderData/FolderResults/FolderFigures are absolute (or render-time-working-directory-relative) paths — the template ships inside an installed package and can be rendered from anywhere. One call renders one report; loop with derive_filtered_annotation() for multi-subset batch runs (see the \dontrun{} example on run_howmahico_report).

Focused reports (instead of the all-in-one 00_mhc_report) — build the pep_all cache once with build_pep_all(), then render any subset of the smaller, purpose-focused templates against it (no re-parsing per report):

annot <- read_annot("1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")
build_pep_all(software = "fragpipe_dda_combined", folder_data = "2_data",
              annotation = annot, shortpep_range = c(8, 13),
              file_rda = "2_data/dda_all_pep_all.rda")

for (tmpl in c("01_id_counts",     # ID counts, size distributions, motifs, PTM
               "02_overlaps",      # replicate / condition / pairwise overlap
               "03_lcms_qc",       # RT/1k0/mz, Score/ppm (advanced)
               "04_quant",         # log2(Area) correlation, Area %CV
               "05_quality_score", # per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score
               "06_quant_stats")) {# differential abundance between Conditions
  run_howmahico_report(tmpl,
                       params = list(SampleSet = "project_id", Subset = "dda_all",
                                     FolderData = "2_data", FolderResults = "3_results",
                                     FolderFigures = "4_figures",
                                     Software = "fragpipe_dda_combined"),
                       output_file = paste0(tmpl, "__dda_all.html"))
}

Each focused report chooses how to obtain pep_all via the PepAllSource param: "cached" (default — load the <Subset>_pep_all.rda cache), "rda" (load an explicit PepAllFile), or "build" (parse the raw search output itself, no separate build_pep_all() call). So to render a single focused report directly from results, pass PepAllSource = "build" (plus Software, AnnotationFile, FolderDocumentation) and skip the build_pep_all() step above.

00_mhc_report (all-in-one) and 00_mhc_upsets are unchanged and still parse the raw files themselves.

06_quant_stats compares peptide Area between Conditions (normalization, data completeness, PCA and clustered/unclustered heatmaps, then per-pair differential abundance with volcano plots and a presence/absence track for condition-exclusive ligands). It uses limma, an optional Bioconductor dependency — install it with BiocManager::install("limma"), or render with StatMethod = "ttest" (and NormMethod = "median") for a Bioconductor-free run; the report falls back to that automatically when limma is missing. Its methods and their justification are documented in the report itself.

Reports are written to output_file (HTML), and result tables/figures are written under <FolderResults>/<subset>/ and <FolderFigures>/<subset>/.
